rail_guard.text: Poole. Trains from every station you have been to, and a short walk to the boats.
The line stops here because the sea starts there. Brunel would have built a bridge. He'd have had opinions about the ferry, too.

poole_fisher.text: Cod to Newfoundland, tea off the boats, and now crossing the Channel in a boat the size of a block of flats. Poole's always been about getting out to sea.
The tide here does something odd. It comes up, stops, dips a little, then comes up again. Double high water. Gives the pilots all the time in the world, if they've the nerve.

poole_scout.text: Brownsea Island's over there, with the red squirrels. Baden-Powell brought twenty boys over in 1907 and said, in effect, 'build a fire and see what happens'. A hundred years later, half the country's been to a Scout camp.
I've forty Cubs coming Saturday. Send help. Or hot dogs.

poole_yachtie.text: I live on Sandbanks. The house is the size of a garden shed, but the land underneath costs about the same as a small country.
The chain ferry's lovely, though. It pulls itself over on a chain, all day, calmly. I find it very soothing. I've been watching it for years.

poole_sailor_je.text: St Helier, Jersey? The cows are golden, the potatoes are royal and the tax is low. Not that you'll be seeing the tax.

poole_sailor_gu.text: Guernsey! Cows, castles and a Frenchman's exile. Hold your hat, it's a fresh crossing.
